audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Saul persecution, Samaria mission, Simon Magus, Peter rebuke, angel/Spirit-guided Ethiopian eunuch encounter, Isaiah reading, baptism, Spirit snatching Philip.

verses.restored: Saul was approving of his killing. In that day great persecution happened against the assembly in Jerusalem, and all were scattered through the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.

familiar.text: And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles.

modern.text: And Saul was there, giving approval to Stephen’s death. On that day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.

original.text: Σαῦλος δὲ ἦν συνευδοκῶν τῇ ἀναιρέσει αὐτοῦ. Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ διωγμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις· πάντες δὲ διεσπάρησαν κατὰ τὰς χώρας τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας πλὴν τῶν ἀποστόλων.

verses.restored: Devout men buried Stephen and made great lamentation over him.

familiar.text: And devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him.

modern.text: God-fearing men buried Stephen and mourned deeply over him.

original.text: συνεκόμισαν δὲ τὸν Στέφανον ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς καὶ ⸀ἐποίησαν κοπετὸν μέγαν ἐπʼ αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: But Saul was ravaging the assembly, entering house by house; dragging off both men and women, he was handing them over to prison.

familiar.text: As for Saul, he made havock of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women committed them to prison.

modern.text: But Saul began to destroy the church. Going from house to house, he dragged off men and women and put them in prison. Philip in Samaria

original.text: Σαῦλος δὲ ἐλυμαίνετο τὴν ἐκκλησίαν κατὰ τοὺς οἴκους εἰσπορευόμενος, σύρων τε ἄνδρας καὶ γυναῖκας παρεδίδου εἰς φυλακήν.

verses.restored: Therefore those scattered went through announcing the good news of the word.

familiar.text: Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word.

modern.text: Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.

original.text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες διῆλθον εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν λόγον.

verses.restored: Philip, going down to the city of Samaria, was proclaiming the Messiah to them.

familiar.text: Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and preached Christ unto them.

modern.text: Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them.

original.text: Φίλιππος δὲ κατελθὼν εἰς ⸀τὴν πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας ἐκήρυσσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν χριστόν.

verses.restored: The crowds with one accord were paying attention to the things spoken by Philip, as they heard and saw the signs he was doing.

familiar.text: And the people with one accord gave heed unto those things which Philip spake, hearing and seeing the miracles which he did.

modern.text: The crowds gave their undivided attention to Philip’s message and to the signs they saw him perform.

original.text: προσεῖχον ⸀δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι τοῖς λεγομένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Φιλίππου ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοὺς καὶ βλέπειν τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει·

verses.restored: For many who had unclean spirits, crying with a great voice, were released; and many paralyzed and lame ones were healed.

familiar.text: For unclean spirits, crying with loud voice, came out of many that were possessed with them: and many taken with palsies, and that were lame, were healed.

modern.text: With loud shrieks, unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed, and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed.

original.text: ⸀πολλοὶ γὰρ τῶν ἐχόντων πνεύματα ἀκάθαρτα βοῶντα φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ⸀ἐξήρχοντο, πολλοὶ δὲ παραλελυμένοι καὶ χωλοὶ ἐθεραπεύθησαν·

verses.restored: There was much joy in that city.

familiar.text: And there was great joy in that city.

modern.text: So there was great joy in that city. Simon the Sorcerer (Deuteronomy 18:9–14)

original.text: ⸂ἐγένετο δὲ⸃ ⸂πολλὴ χαρὰ⸃ ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.

verses.restored: A certain man named Simon had previously practiced magic in the city and amazed the nation of Samaria, saying himself to be someone great.

familiar.text: But there was a certain man, called Simon, which beforetime in the same city used sorcery, and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one:

modern.text: Prior to that time, a man named Simon had practiced sorcery in the city and astounded the people of Samaria. He claimed to be someone great,

original.text: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ὀνόματι Σίμων προϋπῆρχεν ἐν τῇ πόλει μαγεύων καὶ ⸀ἐξιστάνων τὸ ἔθνος τῆς Σαμαρείας, λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτὸν μέγαν,

verses.restored: All were paying attention to him, from small to great, saying, This one is the power of the Divine called Great.

familiar.text: To whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God.

modern.text: and all the people, from the least to the greatest, heeded his words and said, “This man is the divine power called the Great Power.”

original.text: ᾧ προσεῖχον ⸀πάντες ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου λέγοντες· Οὗτός ἐστιν ἡ Δύναμις τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ ⸀καλουμένη Μεγάλη.

verses.restored: They paid attention to him because for a long time he had amazed them with magic arts.

familiar.text: And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries.

modern.text: They paid close attention to him because he had astounded them for a long time with his sorcery.

original.text: προσεῖχον δὲ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸ ἱκανῷ χρόνῳ ταῖς μαγείαις ἐξεστακέναι αὐτούς.

verses.restored: But when they trusted Philip announcing good news concerning the reign of the Divine and the name of Jesus Messiah, they were baptized, both men and women.

familiar.text: But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of God, and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

modern.text: But when they believed Philip as he preached the gospel of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

original.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐπίστευσαν τῷ Φιλίππῳ εὐαγγελιζομένῳ ⸀περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐβαπτίζοντο ἄνδρες τε καὶ γυναῖκες.

verses.restored: Simon himself also trusted, and being baptized, he was continuing with Philip; beholding signs and great powers happening, he was amazed.

familiar.text: Then Simon himself believed also: and when he was baptized, he continued with Philip, and wondered, beholding the miracles and signs which were done.

modern.text: Even Simon himself believed and was baptized. He followed Philip closely and was astounded by the great signs and miracles he observed.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Σίμων καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπίστευσεν, καὶ βαπτισθεὶς ἦν προσκαρτερῶν τῷ Φιλίππῳ, θεωρῶν τε ⸂σημεῖα καὶ δυνάμεις μεγάλας γινομένας⸃ ἐξίστατο.

verses.restored: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Divine, they sent Peter and John to them,

familiar.text: Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:

modern.text: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.

original.text: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀπόστολοι ὅτι δέδεκται ἡ Σαμάρεια τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς ⸀αὐτοὺς Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην,

verses.restored: who, coming down, prayed concerning them that they might receive holy Spirit.

familiar.text: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:

modern.text: On their arrival, they prayed for them to receive the Holy Spirit.

original.text: οἵτινες καταβάντες προσηύξαντο περὶ αὐτῶν ὅπως λάβωσιν πνεῦμα ἅγιον·

verses.restored: For he had not yet fallen upon any of them; they had only been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

familiar.text: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)

modern.text: For the Holy Spirit had not yet fallen upon any of them; they had simply been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

original.text: ⸀οὐδέπω γὰρ ἦν ἐπʼ οὐδενὶ αὐτῶν ἐπιπεπτωκός, μόνον δὲ βεβαπτισμένοι ὑπῆρχον εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ ⸀κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: Then they laid hands upon them, and they received holy Spirit.

familiar.text: Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.

modern.text: Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

original.text: τότε ⸀ἐπετίθεσαν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπʼ αὐτούς, καὶ ἐλάμβανον πνεῦμα ἅγιον.

verses.restored: Simon, seeing that through the laying on of the apostles' hands the Spirit was given, brought them silver,

familiar.text: And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money,

modern.text: When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money.

original.text: ⸀ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Σίμων ὅτι διὰ τῆς ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων δίδοται τὸ ⸀πνεῦμα προσήνεγκεν αὐτοῖς χρήματα

verses.restored: saying, Give me also this authority, so that on whomever I lay hands, that one may receive holy Spirit.

familiar.text: Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost.

modern.text: “Give me this power as well,” he said, “so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.”

original.text: λέγων· Δότε κἀμοὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ᾧ ἐὰν ἐπιθῶ τὰς χεῖρας λαμβάνῃ πνεῦμα ἅγιον.

verses.restored: But Peter said to him, May your silver be with you into ruin, because you thought the gift of the Divine could be acquired through money.

familiar.text: But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.

modern.text: But Peter replied, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!

original.text: Πέτρος δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Τὸ ἀργύριόν σου σὺν σοὶ εἴη εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὅτι τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐνόμισας διὰ χρημάτων κτᾶσθαι.

verses.restored: There is not for you a part or share in this word, for your heart is not straight before the Divine.

familiar.text: Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God.

modern.text: You have no part or share in our ministry, because your heart is not right before God.

original.text: οὐκ ἔστιν σοι μερὶς οὐδὲ κλῆρος ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, ἡ γὰρ καρδία σου οὐκ ἔστιν εὐθεῖα ⸀ἔναντι τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Turn/realign therefore from this harmfulness of yours, and ask the Lord if perhaps the intention of your heart may be released to you.

familiar.text: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.

modern.text: Repent, therefore, of your wickedness, and pray to the Lord. Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart.

original.text: μετανόησον οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας σου ταύτης, καὶ δεήθητι τοῦ ⸀κυρίου εἰ ἄρα ἀφεθήσεταί σοι ἡ ἐπίνοια τῆς καρδίας σου·

verses.restored: For I see you are in bitter gall and bond of injustice.

familiar.text: For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity.

modern.text: For I see that you are poisoned by bitterness and captive to iniquity.”

original.text: εἰς γὰρ χολὴν πικρίας καὶ σύνδεσμον ἀδικίας ὁρῶ σε ὄντα.

verses.restored: Simon answered and said, You ask the Lord for me, so that nothing of what you have said may come upon me.

familiar.text: Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the LORD for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me.

modern.text: Then Simon answered, “Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.”

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Σίμων εἶπεν· Δεήθητε ὑμεῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν κύριον ὅπως μηδὲν ἐπέλθῃ ἐπʼ ἐμὲ ὧν εἰρήκατε.

verses.restored: They therefore, having testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, announcing the good news to many villages of the Samaritans.

familiar.text: And they, when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.

modern.text: And after Peter and John had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many of the Samaritan villages. Philip and the Ethiopian (Isaiah 53:1–8)

original.text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διαμαρτυράμενοι καὶ λαλήσαντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου ⸀ὑπέστρεφον εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα, πολλάς τε κώμας τῶν Σαμαριτῶν ⸀εὐηγγελίζοντο.

verses.restored: A messenger of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, Rise and go toward the south on the road going down from Jerusalem to Gaza; this is wilderness.

familiar.text: And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert.

modern.text: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”

original.text: Ἄγγελος δὲ κυρίου ἐλάλησεν πρὸς Φίλιππον λέγων· Ἀνάστηθι καὶ πορεύου κατὰ μεσημβρίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τὴν καταβαίνουσαν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Γάζαν· αὕτη ἐστὶν ἔρημος.

verses.restored: Rising, he went. Look, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a powerful official of Candace queen of Ethiopians, who was over all her treasury, had come to worship in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship,

modern.text: So he started out, and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,

original.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐπορεύθη, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ Αἰθίοψ εὐνοῦχος δυνάστης ⸀Κανδάκης βασιλίσσης Αἰθιόπων, ὃς ἦν ἐπὶ πάσης τῆς γάζης αὐτῆς, ὃς ἐληλύθει προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,

verses.restored: He was returning and sitting in his chariot, and he was reading the prophet Isaiah.

familiar.text: Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet.

modern.text: and on his return was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.

original.text: ἦν ⸀τε ὑποστρέφων καὶ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ ἅρματος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεγίνωσκεν τὸν προφήτην Ἠσαΐαν.

verses.restored: The Spirit said to Philip, Go near and join yourself to this chariot.

familiar.text: Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot.

modern.text: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go over to that chariot and stay by it.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τῷ Φιλίππῳ· Πρόσελθε καὶ κολλήθητι τῷ ἅρματι τούτῳ.

verses.restored: Running up, Philip heard him reading Isaiah the prophet and said, Do you indeed know what you are reading?

familiar.text: And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?

modern.text: So Philip ran up and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. “Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.

original.text: προσδραμὼν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ ἀναγινώσκοντος ⸂Ἠσαΐαν τὸν προφήτην⸃ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἆρά γε γινώσκεις ἃ ἀναγινώσκεις;

verses.restored: He said, How could I, unless someone guides me? He invited Philip to come up and sit with him.

familiar.text: And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.

modern.text: “How can I,” he said, “unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Πῶς γὰρ ἂν δυναίμην ἐὰν μή τις ⸀ὁδηγήσει με; παρεκάλεσέν τε τὸν Φίλιππον ἀναβάντα καθίσαι σὺν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: The passage of Scripture he was reading was this: As a sheep to slaughter he was led, and as a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he does not open his mouth.

familiar.text: The place of the scripture which he read was this, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth:

modern.text: The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth.

original.text: ἡ δὲ περιοχὴ τῆς γραφῆς ἣν ἀνεγίνωσκεν ἦν αὕτη· Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ ⸀κείραντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: In his humiliation, justice was taken away from him. Who will describe his generation? For his life is taken away from the earth.

familiar.text: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: and who shall declare his generation? for his life is taken from the earth.

modern.text: In His humiliation He was deprived of justice. Who can recount His descendants? For His life was removed from the earth.”

original.text: ἐν τῇ ⸀ταπεινώσει ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη· ⸀τὴν γενεὰν αὐτοῦ τίς διηγήσεται; ὅτι αἴρεται ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: The eunuch answered Philip and said, I ask you, concerning whom does the prophet say this, concerning himself or concerning another?

familiar.text: And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man?

modern.text: “Tell me,” said the eunuch, “who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?”

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ εὐνοῦχος τῷ Φιλίππῳ εἶπεν· Δέομαί σου, περὶ τίνος ὁ προφήτης λέγει ⸀τοῦτο; περὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἢ περὶ ἑτέρου τινός;

verses.restored: Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, announced the good news of Jesus to him.

familiar.text: Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus.

modern.text: Then Philip began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.

original.text: ἀνοίξας δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς γραφῆς ταύτης εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτῷ τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

verses.restored: As they were going along the road, they came upon some water, and the eunuch says, Look, water. What prevents me from being baptized?

familiar.text: And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?

modern.text: As they traveled along the road and came to some water, the eunuch said, “Look, here is water! What is there to prevent me from being baptized?”

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἐπορεύοντο κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἦλθον ἐπί τι ὕδωρ, καί φησιν ὁ εὐνοῦχος· Ἰδοὺ ὕδωρ, τί κωλύει με ⸀βαπτισθῆναι;

verses.restored: [Some later manuscripts add a confession of trust before baptism.]

familiar.text: And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.

modern.note: The BSB follows modern critical-text practice here and does not print this traditional verse number as a separate verse.

original.note: This traditional verse number is not present as a separate verse in the SBLGNT base text; preserve as a textual-witness issue.

verses.restored: He commanded the chariot to stand still, and they both went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.

familiar.text: And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him.

modern.text: And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.

original.text: καὶ ἐκέλευσεν στῆναι τὸ ἅρμα, καὶ κατέβησαν ἀμφότεροι εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ ὅ τε Φίλιππος καὶ ὁ εὐνοῦχος, καὶ ἐβάπτισεν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: When they came up out of the water, Spirit of the Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went on his way rejoicing.

familiar.text: And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.

modern.text: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, but went on his way rejoicing.

original.text: ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβησαν ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος, πνεῦμα κυρίου ἥρπασεν τὸν Φίλιππον, καὶ οὐκ εἶδεν αὐτὸν οὐκέτι ὁ εὐνοῦχος, ἐπορεύετο γὰρ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ χαίρων.

verses.restored: Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through, he announced the good news to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.

familiar.text: But Philip was found at Azotus: and passing through he preached in all the cities, till he came to Caesarea.

modern.text: But Philip appeared at Azotus and traveled through that region, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.

original.text: Φίλιππος δὲ εὑρέθη εἰς Ἄζωτον, καὶ διερχόμενος εὐηγγελίζετο τὰς πόλεις πάσας ἕως τοῦ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν.
